aime-le-vs-bois-du.title: "J'aime LE café" or "je bois DU café"?
aime-le-vs-bois-du.body: With verbs of liking (aimer, détester), you use the definite article to talk about the thing in general: j'aime le café (I like coffee, in general). But when you're talking about an amount — drinking, eating, buying — you use the partitive article: je bois du café (I drink [some] coffee). It's a distinction English doesn't make, but it's essential in French.

croissant-nao-e-diario.title: Croissants every day? Not for most French people
croissant-nao-e-diario.body: There's an idea that French people eat croissants for breakfast every day — but in practice it's more common to save croissants for weekends or special occasions. Day to day, French breakfast is usually simpler: bread with butter/jam (tartine), or just coffee.
examples: bread with butter/jam — the most common breakfast
